clue.text: Country material

definitions.meaning: a nation, the Netherlands by its familiar name
a plain linen fabric, often unbleached, used for blinds and furnishings

explanation.definitionFit: The Netherlands is commonly called by this name, and the same word names a coarse linen cloth.

clue.text: Carry round for sale part of plant

parts.note: to hawk goods is to peddle them
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: A pedlar's wares include part of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-flowered daisy-family weed.

clue.text: Nothing to settle, in Romeo's eyes?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis
to light on something is to settle on it

explanation.surface: Romeo's gaze has no settling place.
explanation.definitionFit: The glow of affection shining in a lover's look, fitting Shakespeare's Romeo.

clue.text: Concur concerning filling in time

indicators.note: filling in says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: an age is a period of time
re means concerning

explanation.surface: Agreement on the matter of filling in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to be of one mind.

clue.text: Erred badly about call for weapon

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go around another piece
badly says the letters of erred are muddled

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: A mistaken summons for a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns ERRED into DERER, and 'about' wraps that round RING.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pocket pistol named after its American maker.

clue.text: Best means of securing the crest

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks
a knot is a way of fastening a rope

explanation.surface: Advice on the finest way to keep hold of a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuft of hair or feathers on the head forms a crest, as on a crested bird.

clue.text: Indian transport in South Pacific

definitions.meaning: a light two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle in India

explanation.definitionFit: A light Indian carriage, and also the Polynesian island kingdom.

clue.text: Such treasures going free? Most amusing

definitions.meaning: treasures with no cost attached, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: Invaluable treasures are literally without cost; informally the word also means hilarious.

clue.text: Girl causes no 'end of a minor disturbance

indicators.note: disturbance says the remaining letters are shaken up
no end of says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the words a minor written out

explanation.surface: A girl creates endless minor fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' drops the R of A MINOR to leave AMINO; 'disturbance' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name from the Book of Ruth.

clue.text: Where we see 11 out of 27

parts.note: a dancer (11) viewed from the upper seats (27) is seen at a playhouse

explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is where a dancer is watched from the upper seats.

clue.text: Hairdresser appears to vacillate

definitions.meaning: one who puts waves into hair

explanation.definitionFit: One who sets waves in hair is literally a waver; to waver is also to dither between options.

clue.text: Reckless person set Russian leader against his European neighbour

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for Russian
anti means against
Poland borders Russia, so a Pole is a Russian's neighbour

explanation.surface: A rash figure sets the Kremlin chief against the man next door in Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like part of the definition but merely tells you to take R from Russian; 'set' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a wild, rakish, harum-scarum individual.

clue.text: Dancer of note to go abroad in mid-May

parts.note: B is a musical note
aller is the French for to go, so the foreign version

indicators.note: mid asks for the central letter of the word May

explanation.surface: A celebrated ballet star sets off on a foreign trip in the middle of May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of note' suggests a famous dancer, but 'note' is just B. 'to go abroad' means 'to go' in a foreign language: French ALLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A female ballet performer is the classic stage dancer.

clue.text: Poet shows the work 'e returned

indicators.note: returned asks for the pieces to be read backwards

parts.note: toil means work, labour
the dropped-aitch 'e stands for he, leaving just E

explanation.surface: A versifier displays the labour he gave back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns TOILE into ELIOT, the poet T. S. Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was a celebrated twentieth-century writer of verse.

clue.text: They were assumed by Romans to talk a lot

definitions.meaning: the robes put on by Roman citizens

explanation.definitionFit: Romans donned these robes; split in two the word also reads as a phrase meaning to chatter.

clue.text: Alias Peter Simple? The real thing

parts.note: the apostle Peter was also called Simon
pure means simple, unmixed

explanation.surface: A character's pseudonym is a naive fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Simple is a naval novel; but Simon was the Apostle Peter's other name.
explanation.definitionFit: A genuine, authentic person or thing, from an 18th-century comedy character.

clue.text: Cricketer to record a piece of music

parts.note: W. G. Grace, the famous Victorian English cricketer
to note is to write down, record

explanation.surface: A sportsman sets down a composition.
explanation.walkthrough: W. G. GRACE was the most famous English cricketer of the 19th century.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental extra tone added to a melody is a small musical item.

clue.text: Denied, by Jack-aged ten, roughly

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, AB an able seaman

indicators.note: roughly says the letters of aged ten are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ten-year-old Jack is turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Renounced, refused oneself.

clue.text: Form of drill received from dentist?

definitions.meaning: a military drill in widely spaced formation
the dentist's instruction to open your mouth

explanation.definitionFit: A loose military formation; humorously, the dentist's 'open' command.

clue.text: Accountant thanks man holding painter of boat

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
ta is British informal thanks

indicators.note: holding says the word man wraps around another piece

parts.note: taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper thanks someone grasping the mooring rope of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'painter' is also a boat's mooring line, a pun that hides RA (Royal Academician).
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-hulled sailing vessel.

clue.text: Dog-fish 'seen on ice

parts.note: a cur is a dog
ling is a fish

explanation.surface: A dogfish spotted on a frozen pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish sport of sliding stones across a frozen surface.

clue.text: Appears to understand the writer's work

parts.note: to see is to understand
MS is a manuscript, an author's work

explanation.surface: Someone seems to grasp an author's output.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe how something looks or comes across.

clue.text: Conchy poet?

parts.note: conchy here means shell-like, so a poet whose name suggests shells

explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe Shelley, the Romantic poet, whose name looks shell-like.

clue.text: Mature writer from the island state?

parts.note: RI is Rhode Island, a US state
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A grown-up author comes from an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, the smallest US state.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow ripe or come to full development.

clue.text: A seer in some form

definitions.meaning: part of the eye through which we see
a student in a school class

explanation.definitionFit: The dark opening of the eye lets one see; a student belongs to a school class.

clue.text: Crew takes part in dance

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew
some means a part of

explanation.surface: A rowing team joins in a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish reel for eight dancers.

clue.text: Time we should attack?

definitions.meaning: old slang: 'how goes the ...?' means what time is it

explanation.definitionFit: Time is jokingly the foe, and an opponent is whom we attack.

clue.text: Paper set up half their leader

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means read upwards

parts.note: semi means half

indicators.note: leader asks for the first letter of the word their

explanation.surface: A newspaper puts up half its chief.
explanation.definitionFit: The London daily newspaper.

clue.text: Cheeky redhead in this is ill-advised

indicators.note: in says the R goes inside the other word

parts.note: this refers back to cheeky, i.e. impudent
the head of red is R

explanation.surface: A saucy redhead behaving rashly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheeky' defines 'this', which is IMPUDENT; R (head of red) goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash, unwise, lacking prudence.

clue.text: " The very of a modern Major-General '"" (Gilbert)

definitions.text: " The very of a modern Major-General '"" (Gilbert)

parts.words: " The very of a modern Major-General '"" (Gilbert)
parts.note: fill in the missing word from the patter song in The Pirates of Penzance by Gilbert and Sullivan

explanation.definitionFit: The song line is 'I am the very model of a modern Major-General', meaning a perfect example.

clue.text: Where pictures are seen of the gods?

definitions.meaning: the highest seats in a theatre

explanation.definitionFit: An art museum room displays paintings; the topmost theatre seats are also called 'the gods'.

clue.text: Ruin for some of the proudest royalists?

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Downfall befalls a few of the haughtiest monarchists.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to wreck it completely.
